question: Should plugin import boundary enforcement ship as a fail-closed loader-time security policy now, or should maintainers require a redesigned enforcement and rollout plan before merge?
rationale: The PR changes plugin trust and compatibility behavior, and the current patch has security-bypass and upgrade risks that require owner intent on the enforcement shape and rollout.

options.title: Redesign before merge
options.body: Keep the PR open and require robust enforcement plus upgrade proof across current loader paths before landing.

options.title: Narrow to diagnostics first
options.body: Convert the change to a warning/reporting mode first, then ship fail-closed enforcement in a later compatibility window.

options.title: Replace with fresh branch
options.body: Start a new branch against current main if preserving this stale loader integration is more expensive than carrying over the useful tests and policy intent.

recommendation.title: Redesign before merge
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open and require robust enforcement plus upgrade proof across current loader paths before landing.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns the PR branch and has recent current-main plugin loader/Jiti history, making him the best first routing candidate for the enforcement-shape decision.
